references.text: Isaiah uses similar imagery about riding on the heights of the earth and enjoying the inheritance of Jacob
Job describes the time of blessing when the rock poured out streams of oil, the same image as oil from the flint
The psalm mentions honey from the rock as God's gift to His people, a direct parallel to honey from the mountain
Describes God's blessing with the finest wheat, linked to the produce of the field
Ezekiel prophesies that Israel's mountains will bear fruit, parallel to the produce of the field
Moses' blessing describes Israel as treading on the heights of the enemy, the same image as riding on the heights of the earth
Amos uses the same expression about treading on the heights of the earth as a sign of God's power
Micah describes the Lord as treading on the heights of the earth, similar imagery
Habakkuk concludes with God making him tread on the high places, a direct parallel to Deuteronomy
The description of the land flowing with milk and honey, linked to honey from the rock
